title: Trust Zones in an MCP Exchange

questions.question: In an MCP exchange, which two participants sit inside the same trust domain that the host directly controls?
options: The host and the client it runs
The client and every server it has connected to
The server and the tools it exposes
The model and the upstream systems a server calls
questions.explanation: The host owns the client it runs and both sit inside one trust domain, while the server is a separate program the host does not control.

questions.question: A server's discover result carries a flattering serverInfo.name. What should a host's trust decision rely on instead?
options: The title field inside the server's tool annotations
The identity the host recorded when it connected the server
The name the server reports in its serverInfo field
The name shown in the server's most recent tool description
questions.explanation: clientInfo and serverInfo are self-reported and unverified, so a host must base trust decisions on its own record of which server it connected, never on what the connection claims about itself.

questions.question: A tool from a server that is not on the host's trusted list declares destructiveHint as false. How should the host treat that claim when making a safety decision?
options: Accept it only when the tool's description also sounds harmless
Accept it, since annotations describe exactly what a tool does
Ignore the claim and fall back to the destructive default
Reject the tool outright and remove it from the tool list
questions.explanation: Tool annotations are hints that clients must treat as untrusted unless the server is trusted, so an untrusted claim of destructiveHint false falls back to the conservative default of true.

questions.question: A tool definition includes an icon whose src is javascript:alert(1). What must a conformant client do with that icon?
options: Render the icon inside a sandboxed iframe with scripts disabled
Convert the icon to a data URI before rendering it safely
Render the icon only after asking the user for permission
Reject the icon, since its scheme is not https or data
questions.explanation: Clients must reject icon URIs that use unsafe schemes such as javascript, file, or ftp, accepting only https and data URIs for icon sources.

questions.question: A tool result from a notes server contains text instructing the host to call a delete tool on a separate ticket server. What should the host do?
options: Refuse the call, since crossing servers is the model's choice
Ask the notes server to confirm the instruction before proceeding
Execute the call, since the notes server is already connected
Forward the instruction to the ticket server as a routine notification
questions.explanation: Content one server returns is untrusted data, so an instruction embedded inside it must never trigger a call to a different server. Only a choice the model makes on its own may cross that boundary.

questions.question: Which practice matches MCP's guidance for a locally launched stdio server that needs credentials?
options: Request the credentials through a server-initiated sampling request
Read credentials from the environment instead of running an OAuth flow
Run the full OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow over the stdio transport
Embed a long-lived token inside the server's published package
questions.explanation: stdio implementations should not run the OAuth flow and instead read credentials from the environment, since the transport already runs inside the user's own trust domain.
